introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - Ordinary Level Examination. Computer Science (0595), Paper 3 (practical), Group Three, June 2019. Duration: two and a half hours. Do all the tasks (Task I, Task II and Task III) specified in this question paper.**

Enter the information required in the shaded boxes. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. All written answers should be provided in the spaces provided in this question booklet. Calculators are NOT allowed.

The booklet reproduced here is the Group Three version (booklet 00/0595/3A/Grp 3); a candidate sits only one group. Task I and Task II are done on a computer (word processor and spreadsheet); Task III is a short programming exercise (C or Pascal).
enonce_intro_markdown:
**TASK I (20 marks)**

The following is an article written by a journalist for publication in a journal.

**Ease of Use of Social Media**

In the modern society, social media is becoming more significant for each business area. What social media can do for business is to make a company better by allowing people to listen, react and build faster and more efficiently than ever before. According to "18 Reasons to Use Social Media" by Lisa Barone, there are 18 reasons to use social media in business, called the advantages of using social media in business.

In the article "Why Do People Use Online Social Networking", Dachary Carey pointed out that online social networking is positive in helping people connect and collaborate at work. In Carey's opinion, social networking enables people keeping in touch with old friends and making new oneself across the miles available. "It's the ultimate networking tool" said Carey. For individual using, Carey concluded that online social networking is a great way to expand your social circle and get in touch with people you otherwise wouldn't speak with regularly.

In the business area, social networking tools are also very useful. Carey mentioned that both employees and employers can get benefits in looking up jobs and hiring staff. Furthermore, social networking also can be used for advertising new products and deals, communicating with customers or anything else. But, Carey still highlighted out that social networking also carries a few negatives, especially for children. He mentioned that parents must be vigilant to ensure kids are still spending quality time with friends in person due to the danger that using online social networking may lead people withdrawing from real life interactions.

*https://www.omicsonline.org/open-access*

questions.enonce_markdown: Name the Word Processor, including the version, installed on your computer. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The answer is read on the computer used, so it cannot be invented here. Open the word processor and note its name and version number (in a word processor of the Microsoft Word family: *File* > *Account* (or *Help*) > *About*; in another suite look in the *Help* > *About* window).

A complete answer has two parts: **the name** of the program (for example *Microsoft Word* or *LibreOffice Writer*) and **its version** (for example the year or the version number shown in the *About* window).

Marking idea (2 marks): name of the word processor (1); version (1).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Open a new word processor document and

a. set the page layout to landscape

b. set margins at 2.5cm on the left, right, top and bottom. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. Open the word processor and start a **blank document** (*File* > *New* > *Blank document*).
2. **Landscape.** *Layout* (or *Page Layout*) tab > *Orientation* > **Landscape**.
3. **Margins.** *Layout* tab > *Margins* > **Custom Margins** (or *Page Setup*), then type **2.5 cm** in each of the four boxes: **Top**, **Bottom**, **Left** and **Right**. Click *OK*.

Check: the page is now wider than it is tall and the four margin boxes show 2.5 cm.

Marking idea (3 marks): new document (1); landscape orientation (1); the four margins set to 2.5 cm (1).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Type (without the borders) the article in Figure 1 with the following formatting: *[4 marks]*

a. The title should be use an ARIAL BOLD, 15 point font, and aligned CENTRED. *[2 marks]*

b. The paragraphs should be TIMES NEW ROMAN, 11 point font and aligned JUSTIFIED *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Typing (4 marks).** Click in the new document and type the title *Ease of Use of Social Media* and the three paragraphs exactly as printed in Figure 1. Do **not** type the box (border) round the article; the web address line under the article is only a source note. Check spelling and punctuation against Figure 1 (quotation marks, the names *Lisa Barone* and *Dachary Carey*, the number *18*). Press *Enter* only between paragraphs, not at the end of each line.

**a. Title (2 marks).** Select the title line, then on the *Home* tab choose the font **Arial**, click **Bold** (*B*), set the size to **15**, and click **Center** (*Ctrl + E*).

**b. Paragraphs (2 marks).** Select the three paragraphs (drag with the mouse, or click in the first one and press *Ctrl + Shift + End*), then choose the font **Times New Roman**, the size **11**, and click **Justify** (*Ctrl + J*). The right edge of each paragraph is now straight.

Marking idea (8 marks in all): text typed correctly without the borders (4); title Arial Bold 15 and centred (2); paragraphs Times New Roman 11 and justified (2).

questions.enonce_markdown: Arrange the first paragraph to have 3 columns, the second paragraph to have 2 columns and the third paragraph to have 3 columns. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. Select the **first paragraph only** (triple-click inside it). *Layout* tab > *Columns* > **Three**.
2. Select the **second paragraph only**. *Layout* > *Columns* > **Two**.
3. Select the **third paragraph only**. *Layout* > *Columns* > **Three**.

When a paragraph is selected before the command, the word processor automatically puts **continuous section breaks** before and after it, so each paragraph can have its own number of columns while the title stays in one column. (If the whole text were selected, all paragraphs would receive the same number of columns, which would be wrong.)

Marking idea (2 marks): paragraph 1 in 3 columns and paragraph 3 in 3 columns (1); paragraph 2 in 2 columns (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Insert a comment in the first paragraph that reads: "*This is written without any publicity*" on the sentence that begins with "According to ....". *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. In the first paragraph, select the sentence that begins **"According to "18 Reasons to Use Social Media" by Lisa Barone, ..."** (from the word *According* to the full stop at the end of that sentence).
2. *Review* tab > **New Comment** (or right-click > *New Comment*).
3. In the comment balloon type exactly: **This is written without any publicity**
4. Click outside the balloon to finish.

The comment must be attached to the sentence that begins with "According to", not to the title or to another paragraph.

Marking idea (3 marks): the right sentence selected (1); comment inserted (1); comment text typed exactly (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Insert a rectangle at the end of a third paragraph into which the journalist will eventually insert his signature. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. Click at the **end of the third paragraph** (after the last word *interactions.*) and press *Enter* so that the rectangle has its own line.
2. *Insert* tab > *Shapes* > **Rectangle** (in the *Basic Shapes* / *Rectangles* group).
3. Drag with the mouse to draw a rectangle of a suitable size (large enough for a signature), placed just below the last line of the third paragraph.
4. Leave it **empty** (no text inside): the journalist will sign in it later. If it has a solid fill that would hide a signature, choose *Shape Fill* > *No Fill* and keep the outline.

Marking idea (2 marks): a rectangle inserted (1); placed at the end of the third paragraph and left empty (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Save your work as Task I.
questions.corrige_markdown: *File* > *Save As* > choose the folder given by the supervisor, type the file name **Task I** and click *Save*.
*File* > *Print*: check the preview (landscape page, three sections with 3, 2 and 3 columns), choose the printer and click *Print*. Insert the printout in the booklet.
